Build a fully operational, production-ready, AI-assisted cloud development platform. The system allows authenticated users to create isolated development workspaces, manage source files within those workspaces, execute shell commands in a real pseudo-terminal, configure declarative package environments, interact with a multi-step AI agent that autonomously edits code and validates its own output via automated browser testing, create and restore named filesystem checkpoints, manage encrypted secrets, and preview running applications through a reverse proxy. Every component must be implemented in two files: a single Node.js backend file (`server.js`) and a single HTML frontend file (`index.html`). A `package.json` and a `.env` file are also required. No other files are permitted. No build tools, transpilers, or bundlers are permitted. All backend logic executes in the single `server.js` process. All frontend logic executes in the browser using the single `index.html` file.

***

## SECTION 1 — SYSTEM OVERVIEW

The system is a browser-accessible cloud development platform that solves the problem of fragmented developer tooling by unifying a code editor, terminal emulator, AI coding agent, declarative environment manager, version-controlled checkpointing system, secrets vault, and live application preview into a single cohesive interface backed by a single server process.

A user registers an account, creates named projects, and is placed into a workspace that presents a file tree, a multi-tab code editor, an integrated terminal, and an AI agent chat panel. The AI agent operates autonomously over multiple iterations using tool calls to read files, write files, execute shell commands, manage snapshots, and validate the running application by generating and executing Playwright test scripts. A lightweight error-pattern classifier runs after each agent iteration and injects context-appropriate micro-instructions into the agent prompt to break repetitive failure loops. Every significant state change can be captured as a named snapshot (implemented as a git commit) and restored atomically. Secrets are stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted in SQLite and injected as environment variables into all terminal and command-execution contexts for the owning project.

***

## SECTION 2 — COMPLETE DATA MODEL

All persistent data is stored in a SQLite database file located at the path specified by the environment variable `DB_PATH`. The database is opened with WAL journal mode enabled. All tables are created on server startup if they do not exist. No ORM is used; all queries use the `better-sqlite3` synchronous API directly.

### Table: `users`

```
id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
email       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
password_hash TEXT NOT NULL   -- bcrypt, 12 rounds
created_at  TEXT NOT NULL     -- ISO 8601 UTC
updated_at  TEXT NOT NULL     -- ISO 8601 UTC
```

### Table: `projects`

```
id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
name        TEXT NOT NULL     -- max 100 chars, non-empty after trim
description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
root_path   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE  -- absolute filesystem path to workspace dir
created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
updated_at  TEXT NOT NULL
```

### Table: `refresh_tokens`

```
id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
token_hash  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE  -- SHA-256 hex of the raw token
expires_at  TEXT NOT NULL     -- ISO 8601 UTC, 7 days from creation
created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
```

### Table: `snapshots`

```
id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
project_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
label       TEXT NOT NULL     -- user-provided label, max 200 chars
git_hash    TEXT NOT NULL     -- full 40-char SHA-1 git commit hash
created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
```

### Table: `secrets`

```
id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
project_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
key_name        TEXT NOT NULL     -- max 100 chars, uppercase letters/digits/underscores only, regex: /^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,99}$/
encrypted_value TEXT NOT NULL     -- AES-256-GCM; format: iv_hex:authTag_hex:ciphertext_hex
created_at      TEXT NOT NULL
updated_at      TEXT NOT NULL
UNIQUE(project_id, key_name)
```

### Table: `agent_sessions`

```
id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
project_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)
status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'idle'  -- 'idle' | 'running' | 'done' | 'error'
created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
updated_at  TEXT NOT NULL
```

### Table: `agent_messages`

```
id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
session_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES agent_sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
role        TEXT NOT NULL     -- 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool'
content     TEXT NOT NULL     -- JSON string for tool results; plain text for user/assistant
tool_call_id TEXT             -- NULL unless role='tool'; links to agent_tool_calls.id
created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
```

### Table: `agent_tool_calls`

```
id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
message_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES agent_messages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
tool_name   TEXT NOT NULL
tool_args   TEXT NOT NULL     -- JSON string
tool_result TEXT NOT NULL     -- JSON string
created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
```

### Table: `process_registry`

```
id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY  -- UUID v4
project_id  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
pid         INTEGER NOT NULL
port        INTEGER           -- NULL if not yet detected
command     TEXT NOT NULL
started_at  TEXT NOT NULL
```

This table is cleared on server startup. It tracks which project has a foreground process currently running for the live preview feature.

### Filesystem Layout

Each project is assigned a root path at `PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/{project_id}/workspace/`. A git repository is initialized at `PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/{project_id}/workspace/` using `git init`. A `.gitignore` file is written to that directory on project creation containing `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/`, `.env`, `*.pyc`, `dist/`, `.cache/`. An `environment.json` file is written at the workspace root with default content `{"language":"node","packages":{"npm":[],"pip":[],"gem":[],"go":[]},"startCommand":"","envVars":{}}` and is immediately committed as the initial git commit with message `"Initial commit"`.

***

## SECTION 3 — BACKEND IMPLEMENTATION (`server.js`)

### 3.1 Dependencies and Initialization

The file begins with `require('dotenv').config()`. All imports follow immediately. The required npm packages are: `express`, `ws`, `better-sqlite3`, `node-pty`, `jsonwebtoken`, `bcryptjs`, `uuid` (v4), `node-fetch`, `simple-git`, `http-proxy`, `crypto` (Node built-in), `path` (Node built-in), `fs` (Node built-in), `child_process` (Node built-in), `http` (Node built-in), `os` (Node built-in).

The Express application is created. A raw HTTP server is created from the Express app using `http.createServer(app)`. The WebSocket server is attached to the HTTP server using `new WebSocketServer({ server: httpServer, path: undefined })` so that all WebSocket upgrades are routed through a single `wss` instance. The WebSocket server's connection handler reads `request.url` and routes each connection to the appropriate handler function based on URL pattern matching.

### 3.2 Middleware

Apply to all routes in order:
1. `express.json()` with a body size limit of `'2mb'`
2. A custom CORS middleware that reads `CORS_ORIGIN` from environment (defaults to `'*'`), sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization`, and `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS`. Respond to `OPTIONS` preflight requests with status 204 immediately.
3. A request logger that writes `[METHOD] PATH STATUS TIME_MS` to stdout for every response.

### 3.3 Authentication Utilities

**`hashPassword(password)`**: Uses `bcryptjs.hash(password, 12)`.

**`verifyPassword(password, hash)`**: Uses `bcryptjs.compare(password, hash)`.

**`generateAccessToken(userId)`**: Signs `{sub: userId, type: 'access'}` with `JWT_SECRET`, expiry `'15m'`.

**`generateRefreshToken()`**: Returns a 64-byte random hex string via `crypto.randomBytes(64).toString('hex')`.

**`hashToken(token)`**: Returns `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex')`.

**`encryptSecret(plaintext)`**: Generates a random 12-byte IV. Derives a 32-byte key from `SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` using `crypto.scryptSync(SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY, 'static-salt-v1', 32)`. Creates an AES-256-GCM cipher. Encrypts `plaintext`. Returns `iv_hex + ':' + authTag_hex + ':' + ciphertext_hex`.

**`decryptSecret(stored)`**: Splits on `:`, reconstructs IV, auth tag, and ciphertext hex, deciphers with AES-256-GCM, returns plaintext string. Throws if authentication fails.

**`authenticateRequest(req, res, next)`**: Reads the `Authorization` header, expects `Bearer <token>`. Verifies with `JWT_SECRET`. Expects `decoded.type === 'access'`. Sets `req.userId = decoded.sub`. Calls `next()`. On any error, responds 401 with `{error: "Unauthorized"}`.

**`requireProjectAccess(req, res, next)`**: Reads `req.params.projectId`. Queries `projects` table for `id = req.params.projectId AND user_id = req.userId`. If not found, responds 404 with `{error: "Project not found"}`. Sets `req.project` to the row. Calls `next()`.

### 3.4 Route Definitions

All route handlers below must follow this error handling convention: wrap all async logic in try-catch; on unexpected error, log the full stack trace to stderr and respond 500 with `{error: "Internal server error"}`. All input validation failures respond 400 with `{error: "<specific validation message>"}`.

***

#### POST `/api/auth/register`

Request body: `{email: string, password: string}`.

Validation:
- `email` must be a non-empty string matching `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/`. If not, 400 `{error: "Invalid email address"}`.
- `password` must be a string with length ≥ 8. If not, 400 `{error: "Password must be at least 8 characters"}`.

Logic:
- Check if a user with the given email already exists. If yes, 409 `{error: "Email already registered"}`.
- Hash the password. Create a new user row with UUID id, trimmed lowercase email, hash, and current UTC ISO timestamps.
- Generate access token and refresh token. Hash refresh token. Insert refresh token row with 7-day expiry.
- Respond 201 `{user: {id, email, created_at}, accessToken: string, refreshToken: string}`.

***

#### POST `/api/auth/login`

Request body: `{email: string, password: string}`.

Validation: same non-empty checks as register.

Logic:
- Find user by lowercase email. If not found, 401 `{error: "Invalid credentials"}`.
- Verify password. If mismatch, 401 `{error: "Invalid credentials"}`.
- Delete all expired refresh tokens for this user from DB.
- Generate new access and refresh tokens. Insert refresh token row.
- Respond 200 `{user: {id, email, created_at}, accessToken: string, refreshToken: string}`.

***

#### POST `/api/auth/refresh`

Request body: `{refreshToken: string}`.

Validation: `refreshToken` must be a non-empty string.

Logic:
- Hash the provided refresh token. Find row by `token_hash`. If not found, 401 `{error: "Invalid refresh token"}`.
- Check if `expires_at` is in the past. If expired, delete the row and respond 401 `{error: "Refresh token expired"}`.
- Delete the current refresh token row (rotation: single use).
- Generate new access token and new refresh token. Insert new refresh token row.
- Respond 200 `{accessToken: string, refreshToken: string}`.

***

#### POST `/api/auth/logout`

Request body: `{refreshToken: string}`.

Logic:
- Hash the token. Delete matching row from `refresh_tokens`. Respond 200 `{message: "Logged out"}` regardless of whether a row was found.

***

#### GET `/api/projects`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`.

Logic: Query all projects where `user_id = req.userId`, ordered by `created_at DESC`. Respond 200 `{projects: [{id, name, description, created_at, updated_at}]}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`.

Request body: `{name: string, description?: string}`.

Validation:
- `name` must be a non-empty string after trim, max 100 chars. If not, 400.
- `description` defaults to empty string if omitted.

Logic:
- Generate project UUID. Compute `root_path = path.join(PROJECTS_BASE_DIR, id, 'workspace')`.
- Create the directory synchronously with `fs.mkdirSync(root_path, {recursive: true})`.
- Write `.gitignore` as described in Section 2 filesystem layout.
- Write `environment.json` with default content as described.
- Initialize git: use `simple-git(root_path)`. Call `git.init()`, then `git.addConfig('user.email', 'agent@platform.local')`, `git.addConfig('user.name', 'Platform Agent')`, then `git.add('.')`, then `git.commit('Initial commit')`.
- Insert project row into DB.
- Respond 201 `{project: {id, name, description, root_path, created_at, updated_at}}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Respond 200 `{project: {id, name, description, root_path, created_at, updated_at}}`.

***

#### PUT `/api/projects/:projectId`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{name?: string, description?: string}`. At least one field must be provided.

Validation: If `name` provided, it must be non-empty after trim, max 100 chars.

Logic: Update the `projects` row, set `updated_at` to now. Respond 200 with updated project object.

***

#### DELETE `/api/projects/:projectId`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic:
- Kill any running process for this project from `process_registry` in-memory map (send `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after 2 seconds if still alive).
- Delete all WebSocket connections associated with this project from in-memory maps.
- Delete the `PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/{projectId}` directory recursively using `fs.rmSync(path, {recursive: true, force: true})`.
- Delete the project row from DB (cascade deletes all snapshots, secrets, agent sessions).
- Respond 200 `{message: "Project deleted"}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId/files`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Query param: `path` (string, optional, defaults to `''` meaning root of workspace).

Logic:
- Resolve the absolute path as `path.resolve(req.project.root_path, query_path)`. Verify it starts with `req.project.root_path` (path traversal prevention). If not, 400 `{error: "Invalid path"}`.
- If path does not exist, 404 `{error: "Path not found"}`.
- If path is a file, return 200 `{type: "file", path: relative_path, size: bytes}`.
- If path is a directory, read directory entries. For each entry, return `{name, type: "file"|"directory", path: relative_path, size: bytes_or_null}`. Do not recurse. Sort: directories first alphabetically, then files alphabetically. Respond 200 `{type: "directory", path: relative_path, entries: [...]}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId/files/content`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Query param: `path` (required, non-empty string).

Logic:
- Resolve and validate path (traversal check). Must be an existing regular file.
- If file size exceeds 5 MB, respond 413 `{error: "File too large to display (max 5 MB)"}`.
- Read file as UTF-8. If reading fails due to binary content (invalid UTF-8), respond 415 `{error: "File is binary and cannot be displayed as text"}`.
- Respond 200 `{path: relative_path, content: string, size: bytes}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects/:projectId/files`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{path: string, type: "file"|"directory", content?: string}`.

Validation:
- `path` must be a non-empty string.
- `type` must be `"file"` or `"directory"`.
- If `type === "file"`, `content` defaults to `''`.

Logic:
- Resolve and validate path (traversal check).
- If the path already exists, 409 `{error: "Path already exists"}`.
- Ensure parent directory exists with `fs.mkdirSync(parentDir, {recursive: true})`.
- If `type === "directory"`: `fs.mkdirSync(absolutePath, {recursive: true})`.
- If `type === "file"`: `fs.writeFileSync(absolutePath, content, 'utf8')`.
- Broadcast file change event over presence WebSocket to all project subscribers.
- Respond 201 `{path: relative_path, type}`.

***

#### PUT `/api/projects/:projectId/files/content`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{path: string, content: string}`.

Logic:
- Resolve and validate path (traversal check).
- If path does not exist or is a directory, 404.
- Write content atomically: write to a temp file in the same directory, then rename.
- Broadcast file change event over presence WebSocket.
- Respond 200 `{path: relative_path, size: bytes}`.

***

#### DELETE `/api/projects/:projectId/files`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Query param: `path` (required).

Logic:
- Resolve and validate path (traversal check).
- If path does not exist, 404.
- Prevent deletion of `environment.json` at root: respond 400 `{error: "Cannot delete environment.json"}`.
- `fs.rmSync(absolutePath, {recursive: true, force: true})`.
- Broadcast file deletion event over presence WebSocket.
- Respond 200 `{message: "Deleted"}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects/:projectId/files/rename`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{from: string, to: string}`.

Logic:
- Resolve and validate both paths (traversal check on both).
- If `from` does not exist, 404.
- If `to` already exists, 409.
- `fs.renameSync(absoluteFrom, absoluteTo)`.
- Broadcast rename event over presence WebSocket.
- Respond 200 `{from: relative_from, to: relative_to}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId/environment`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic:
- Read `environment.json` from workspace root. Parse and respond 200 `{environment: parsed_object}`.

***

#### PUT `/api/projects/:projectId/environment`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{environment: object}`.

Validation:
- `environment.language` must be one of `"node"`, `"python"`, `"ruby"`, `"go"`, `"shell"`.
- `environment.packages` must be an object containing only arrays.
- `environment.startCommand` must be a string (may be empty).
- `environment.envVars` must be an object with string keys and string values.

Logic:
- Serialize to JSON with 2-space indentation and write to `environment.json` in workspace root.
- Determine which package managers to invoke based on `language` and `packages`:
  - `node`: if `packages.npm.length > 0`, run `npm install --save ${packages.npm.join(' ')}` in workspace root.
  - `python`: if `packages.pip.length > 0`, run `pip install ${packages.pip.join(' ')}` in workspace root.
  - `ruby`: if `packages.gem.length > 0`, run `gem install ${packages.gem.join(' ')}` in workspace root.
  - `go`: if `packages.go.length > 0`, run `go get ${packages.go.join(' ')}` in workspace root.
- Run each install command as a child process using `child_process.spawnSync` with a 120-second timeout, capturing stdout and stderr.
- If any install command exits with a non-zero code, respond 422 `{error: "Package installation failed", details: {stdout, stderr}}`.
- On success, respond 200 `{environment: parsed_object, installOutput: {stdout, stderr}}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId/snapshots`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic: Query all snapshots for `project_id`, ordered by `created_at DESC`. Respond 200 `{snapshots: [{id, label, git_hash, created_at}]}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects/:projectId/snapshots`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{label: string}`.

Validation: `label` must be non-empty after trim, max 200 chars.

Logic:
- Using `simple-git(workspace_path)`: run `git.add('.')`, then `git.commit(label, {'--allow-empty': null})`.
- Get the resulting commit hash from the `git.log(['-1'])` result `.latest.hash`.
- Insert snapshot row into DB with the label and hash.
- Respond 201 `{snapshot: {id, label, git_hash, created_at}}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects/:projectId/snapshots/:snapshotId/restore`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic:
- Find snapshot by `id = req.params.snapshotId AND project_id = req.project.id`. If not found, 404.
- Kill any running process for this project (same logic as DELETE project).
- Using `simple-git(workspace_path)`: run `git.checkout(snapshot.git_hash, ['--', '.'])`. This restores the workspace files to the state at that commit without changing HEAD.
- Broadcast full file tree refresh event over presence WebSocket.
- Respond 200 `{message: "Restored", snapshot: {id, label, git_hash, created_at}}`.

***

#### DELETE `/api/projects/:projectId/snapshots/:snapshotId`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic:
- Find snapshot row. If not found, 404.
- Delete the snapshot row from DB. The git commit is retained in history; only the named reference is removed from the platform's view.
- Respond 200 `{message: "Snapshot reference deleted"}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId/secrets`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic: Query all secrets for `project_id`. Return only `{id, key_name, created_at, updated_at}` — never return `encrypted_value`. Respond 200 `{secrets: [...]}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects/:projectId/secrets`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{key_name: string, value: string}`.

Validation:
- `key_name` must match `/^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,99}$/`. If not, 400 `{error: "Secret key must be uppercase with letters, digits, and underscores only"}`.
- `value` must be a string, max 10000 chars.
- If a secret with this `key_name` already exists for this project, 409.

Logic:
- Encrypt value. Insert row. Respond 201 `{secret: {id, key_name, created_at, updated_at}}`.

***

#### PUT `/api/projects/:projectId/secrets/:secretId`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{value: string}`.

Logic:
- Find secret by `id = req.params.secretId AND project_id = req.project.id`. If not found, 404.
- Encrypt new value. Update row `encrypted_value` and `updated_at`. Respond 200 `{secret: {id, key_name, updated_at}}`.

***

#### DELETE `/api/projects/:projectId/secrets/:secretId`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic:
- Find secret, if not found 404. Delete row. Respond 200 `{message: "Secret deleted"}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId/agent/sessions`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic: Query sessions for `project_id` ordered by `created_at DESC`. Respond 200 `{sessions: [{id, status, created_at, updated_at}]}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects/:projectId/agent/sessions`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic: Insert new agent session with `status = 'idle'`. Respond 201 `{session: {id, status, created_at}}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId/agent/sessions/:sessionId`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic:
- Find session by `id` and `project_id`. If not found, 404.
- Query all `agent_messages` for this session ordered by `created_at ASC`. For each message with `role = 'assistant'` that has tool calls, also query `agent_tool_calls` linked to that message.
- Respond 200 `{session: {id, status, created_at, updated_at}, messages: [{id, role, content, tool_calls: [{tool_name, tool_args, tool_result}], created_at}]}`.

***

#### GET `/api/projects/:projectId/process`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic: Check in-memory `processRegistry` Map for `req.project.id`. If entry exists, respond 200 `{running: true, port: number_or_null, pid: number, command: string}`. Otherwise respond 200 `{running: false}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects/:projectId/process/start`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Request body: `{command?: string}`.

Logic:
- If a process already running for this project, respond 409 `{error: "A process is already running"}`.
- Read `environment.json` to get `startCommand` and `envVars`. If `command` is provided in body, override `startCommand`.
- If final command is empty string, respond 400 `{error: "No start command configured"}`.
- Decrypt and load all project secrets into an object.
- Spawn process using `child_process.spawn(command, [], {shell: true, cwd: workspace_path, env: {...process.env, ...envVars, ...decryptedSecrets}})`.
- Track in in-memory `processRegistry` Map: `{pid, port: null, command, started_at: ISO_now}`. Also insert into `process_registry` DB table.
- Attempt to detect port: scan stdout/stderr output for patterns matching `listening on.*:(\d+)` or `port (\d+)` or `:(\d+)`. Once detected, update `port` in both in-memory map and DB.
- Pipe process stdout and stderr over all active presence WebSocket connections for this project as `{type: "process_output", stream: "stdout"|"stderr", data: string}`.
- On process exit, remove from in-memory map and DB, broadcast `{type: "process_exit", code: exit_code}`.
- Respond 200 `{message: "Process started", pid: number}`.

***

#### POST `/api/projects/:projectId/process/stop`

Middleware: `authenticateRequest`, `requireProjectAccess`.

Logic:
- Find process in in-memory map. If none, 404.
- Send `SIGTERM`. After 3 seconds, if still alive, `SIGKILL`.
- Remove from in-memory map and DB immediately. Respond 200 `{message: "Process stopped"}`.

***

#### GET `/preview/:projectId/*`

No authentication required (preview is publicly accessible by design).

Logic:
- Find project in DB by `projectId`. If not found, 404.
- Check in-memory `processRegistry` for this project. If no process running or `port` is null, respond 503 with HTML body: `<html><body style="font-family:sans-serif;padding:2rem"><h2>No process running</h2><p>Start your application using the Run button in the workspace.</p></body></html>`.
- Extract the trailing path after `/preview/{projectId}` and forward the request to `` using `http-proxy`. Set `X-Forwarded-Host` header to the original request host. If proxy fails, respond 502.

### 3.5 WebSocket Handler

The single WebSocket server receives all upgrade connections. In the `connection` event handler, parse `request.url`. Route by pattern:

**Pattern `/ws/terminal/:projectId`:** Call `handleTerminalWs(ws, request, projectId)`.

**Pattern `/ws/agent/:projectId/:sessionId`:** Call `handleAgentWs(ws, request, projectId, sessionId)`.

**Pattern `/ws/presence/:projectId`:** Call `handlePresenceWs(ws, request, projectId)`.

**Any other pattern:** Close the WebSocket with code 4004.

All three handlers begin with identical authentication:
- Parse `token` from URL query string.
- Verify JWT with `JWT_SECRET`. Expect `type === 'access'`. Extract `userId`.
- Query user from DB. If not found, close with code 4001.
- Store `userId` in the `ws` object as `ws.userId`.

***

#### `handleTerminalWs(ws, request, projectId)`

After auth:
- Query project by `projectId AND user_id = userId`. If not found, close with code 4004.
- Decrypt all project secrets for this project.
- Read `environment.json`, extract `envVars`.
- Spawn a `node-pty` pseudo-terminal: `pty.spawn('bash', [], {name: 'xterm-256color', cols: 80, rows: 24, cwd: workspace_path, env: {...process.env, ...envVars, ...decryptedSecrets}})`.
- Store the pty instance in an in-memory Map keyed by a generated connection ID.
- `pty.on('data', data => ws.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'output', data})))`.
- On `ws.message` event: parse JSON. If `{type: 'input', data: string}`, write to pty. If `{type: 'resize', cols: number, rows: number}`, call `pty.resize(cols, rows)`. If `{type: 'ping'}`, send `{type: 'pong'}`.
- On `ws.close` event: kill the pty process. Remove from map.
- On pty exit: send `{type: 'exit', code: exit_code}` and close the WebSocket.

***

#### `handlePresenceWs(ws, request, projectId)`

After auth:
- Query project by `projectId AND user_id = userId`. If not found, close.
- Register `ws` in an in-memory Map: `presenceMap.get(projectId)` is a `Set<WebSocket>`. Add this `ws` to the set. Create the set if it does not exist.
- Send initial message: `{type: 'connected', userId}`.
- On `ws.message` event: parse JSON.
  - If `{type: 'cursor', file: string, line: number, col: number}`: broadcast to all other WebSocket connections in the same project set: `{type: 'peer_cursor', userId, file, line, col}`.
  - If `{type: 'ping'}`: respond `{type: 'pong'}`.
- On `ws.close` event: remove from presence set. If set becomes empty, delete the map entry.

***

#### `handleAgentWs(ws, request, projectId, sessionId)`

After auth:
- Query project by `projectId AND user_id = userId`. If not found, close.
- Query agent session by `sessionId AND project_id = projectId`. If not found, close.
- If session `status === 'running'`, send `{type: 'error', message: 'Session is already running'}` and close.
- On `ws.message` event: parse JSON. If `{type: 'message', content: string}`:
  - Validate `content` is a non-empty string, max 32000 chars.
  - Set session `status = 'running'`, `updated_at = now`.
  - Insert an `agent_messages` row with `role = 'user'`, `content`.
  - Call `runAgentLoop(ws, project, session, content)` asynchronously (do not await in the message handler; it runs concurrently).
- On `ws.close` event: if session is still `status = 'running'`, set it to `status = 'error'`.

### 3.6 Agent Loop (`runAgentLoop`)

This is the core AI execution engine. It is an async function that receives `(ws, project, session, userMessageContent)`.

**Setup:**
- Load all existing `agent_messages` for this session from DB, ordered by `created_at ASC`.
- Decrypt and load all project secrets. Read `environment.json`.
- Define the `messages` array starting with a system message (see below), followed by all historical messages, and the new user message appended at the end.

**System Message Content:**
```
You are an autonomous software engineering agent operating inside a sandboxed cloud development workspace. Your job is to fulfill the user's development request by taking actions using the available tools. You can read and write files, execute shell commands, manage snapshots, configure the environment, and test the running application.

Always work step by step. Before writing code, read existing relevant files first. After making changes, verify they work by running commands. If a command fails, read the error carefully and fix the root cause before retrying. Create a snapshot before making large changes. Test the application by running it and using browser tests to verify correctness.

The workspace path is: {workspace_path}
Current language: {environment.language}
Installed packages: {JSON.stringify(environment.packages)}
Start command: {environment.startCommand || "not configured"}

Rules:
- Never delete environment.json.
- Always validate that the application actually works before declaring completion.
- When you complete the task, end your response with exactly the phrase: TASK COMPLETE.
```

**Tool Definitions (OpenAI function calling format):**

Define the following 11 tools in the `tools` array passed to the OpenAI API:

1. **`read_file`** — Parameters: `{path: {type:"string",description:"Relative path to file from workspace root"}}`. Required: `[path]`.

2. **`write_file`** — Parameters: `{path:{type:"string"}, content:{type:"string",description:"Full file content to write"}}`. Required: `[path, content]`.

3. **`list_files`** — Parameters: `{path:{type:"string",description:"Relative directory path, or empty string for root"}, recursive:{type:"boolean",description:"Whether to recurse into subdirectories"}}`. Required: `[path]`.

4. **`delete_file`** — Parameters: `{path:{type:"string"}}`. Required: `[path]`.

5. **`run_command`** — Parameters: `{command:{type:"string"}, timeout_seconds:{type:"integer",description:"Max execution time, 1–120 seconds",minimum:1,maximum:120}}`. Required: `[command]`.

6. **`search_files`** — Parameters: `{query:{type:"string",description:"Text or regex pattern to search for"}, path:{type:"string",description:"Directory to search in, defaults to workspace root"}, file_pattern:{type:"string",description:"Glob pattern for file names, e.g. '*.js'"}}`. Required: `[query]`.

7. **`create_snapshot`** — Parameters: `{label:{type:"string",description:"Descriptive label for this snapshot"}}`. Required: `[label]`.

8. **`restore_snapshot`** — Parameters: `{snapshot_id:{type:"string",description:"The snapshot UUID to restore to"}}`. Required: `[snapshot_id]`.

9. **`set_environment`** — Parameters: `{language:{type:"string",enum:["node","python","ruby","go","shell"]}, packages:{type:"object"}, start_command:{type:"string"}, env_vars:{type:"object"}}`. Required: `[language]`.

10. **`list_snapshots`** — Parameters: `{}`. Required: `[]`.

11. **`run_browser_test`** — Parameters: `{test_code:{type:"string",description:"Complete Playwright JavaScript test code to execute"}, base_url:{type:"string",description:"The base URL of the running application to test"}}`. Required: `[test_code, base_url]`.

**Tool Execution Functions:**

`execute_read_file(project, args)`: Resolve path, validate traversal. Read up to 5 MB. Return `{success:true, content:string, size:bytes}` or `{success:false, error:string}`.

`execute_write_file(project, args)`: Resolve path, validate traversal. Create parent dirs. Write file. Return `{success:true, bytes_written:number}` or `{success:false, error:string}`.

`execute_list_files(project, args)`: Resolve path, validate traversal. If `recursive` is false or omitted, list one level. If `recursive` is true, walk directory tree up to depth 8, up to 500 entries. Return `{success:true, entries:[{path,type,size}]}` or `{success:false, error:string}`.

`execute_delete_file(project, args)`: Resolve and validate. Block deletion of `environment.json`. Use `fs.rmSync` recursive. Return `{success:true}` or `{success:false, error:string}`.

`execute_run_command(project, args)`: Decrypt secrets. Read environment envVars. Run `child_process.spawnSync(command, [], {shell:true, cwd:workspace_path, env:{...process.env, ...envVars, ...secrets}, timeout:(timeout_seconds||30)*1000, maxBuffer:1024*1024*2})`. Return `{success:true, stdout:string, stderr:string, exit_code:number}`. If timed out, return `{success:false, error:"Command timed out after N seconds"}`.

`execute_search_files(project, args)`: Run `grep -rn --include=<file_pattern> <query> <path>` via `execute_run_command`. Parse output. Return `{success:true, matches:[{file,line,text}], total_count:number}`.

`execute_create_snapshot(project, args)`: Use `simple-git`. Add all, commit with label. Insert DB row. Return `{success:true, snapshot_id:string, git_hash:string}`.

`execute_restore_snapshot(project, args)`: Query DB for snapshot. Use `simple-git`, checkout files to that hash. Return `{success:true}` or `{success:false, error:string}`.

`execute_set_environment(project, args)`: Build environment object from args. Merge with existing environment.json (new values override). Write file. Run package installs. Return `{success:true, install_output:string}` or `{success:false, error:string}`.

`execute_list_snapshots(project, args)`: Query DB for all snapshots. Return `{success:true, snapshots:[{id,label,git_hash,created_at}]}`.

`execute_run_browser_test(project, args)`: Write test code to a temp file at `workspace_path/.platform_tmp/test_${uuid}.mjs`. Run `node {tempfile}` via `execute_run_command` with a 60-second timeout. Delete temp file after execution. Return `{success: exit_code===0, stdout, stderr, exit_code}`.

**The Iteration Loop:**

```
let iteration = 0;
const MAX_ITERATIONS = 40;

while (iteration < MAX_ITERATIONS) {
  iteration++;

  // DTG: Analyze recent tool results for error patterns
  const dtgInstruction = classifyTrajectory(messages);
  const messagesForApi = dtgInstruction
    ? [...messages, {role: 'system', content: dtgInstruction}]
    : messages;

  // Emit thinking indicator
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'thinking', iteration}));

  // Call OpenAI
  const response = await callOpenAI(messagesForApi, tools);

  // Handle streaming or non-streaming response
  // Emit text deltas as they arrive: ws.send({type:'text_delta', delta:string})

  const assistantMessage = response.choices[0].message;

  // Persist assistant message
  const assistantMsgId = uuid();
  insertAgentMessage(session.id, 'assistant', assistantMessage.content || '', null, assistantMsgId);

  // Append to messages array
  messages.push(assistantMessage);

  // If no tool calls and content contains "TASK COMPLETE"
  if (!assistantMessage.tool_calls && assistantMessage.content?.includes('TASK COMPLETE')) {
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'done', reason: 'task_complete'}));
    updateSessionStatus(session.id, 'done');
    return;
  }

  // If no tool calls at all
  if (!assistantMessage.tool_calls || assistantMessage.tool_calls.length === 0) {
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'done', reason: 'agent_stopped'}));
    updateSessionStatus(session.id, 'done');
    return;
  }

  // Execute tool calls
  const toolResultMessages = [];
  for (const toolCall of assistantMessage.tool_calls) {
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({type:'tool_start', tool:toolCall.function.name, args:JSON.parse(toolCall.function.arguments), call_id:toolCall.id}));

    const args = JSON.parse(toolCall.function.arguments);
    let result;
    switch (toolCall.function.name) {
      case 'read_file':        result = await execute_read_file(project, args); break;
      case 'write_file':       result = await execute_write_file(project, args); break;
      case 'list_files':       result = await execute_list_files(project, args); break;
      case 'delete_file':      result = await execute_delete_file(project, args); break;
      case 'run_command':      result = await execute_run_command(project, args); break;
      case 'search_files':     result = await execute_search_files(project, args); break;
      case 'create_snapshot':  result = await execute_create_snapshot(project, args); break;
      case 'restore_snapshot': result = await execute_restore_snapshot(project, args); break;
      case 'set_environment':  result = await execute_set_environment(project, args); break;
      case 'list_snapshots':   result = await execute_list_snapshots(project, args); break;
      case 'run_browser_test': result = await execute_run_browser_test(project, args); break;
      default: result = {success:false, error:`Unknown tool: ${toolCall.function.name}`};
    }

    const resultStr = JSON.stringify(result);
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({type:'tool_result', call_id:toolCall.id, result}));

    // Persist tool call
    const toolCallId = uuid();
    insertToolCall(assistantMsgId, toolCall.function.name, toolCall.function.arguments, resultStr, toolCallId);

    // Persist tool result message
    const toolMsgId = uuid();
    insertAgentMessage(session.id, 'tool', resultStr, toolCallId, toolMsgId);

    toolResultMessages.push({role:'tool', tool_call_id:toolCall.id, content:resultStr});
  }

  messages.push(...toolResultMessages);
}

// Max iterations reached
ws.send(JSON.stringify({type:'error', message:'Maximum iteration limit of 40 reached.'}));
updateSessionStatus(session.id, 'error');
```

**Decision-Time Guidance Classifier (`classifyTrajectory(messages)`):**

Examines the last 6 messages in the messages array. Looks for tool result messages (`role === 'tool'`) only. Applies the following rules in order, returning the first matching micro-instruction string or `null` if none match:

- If any tool result contains `"npm ERR!"` or `"npm warn"` → return `"A package installation error was detected. Read the full error message carefully. Verify the package name is spelled correctly on npmjs.com before retrying. Consider using a specific version number."`
- If any tool result contains `"SyntaxError"` or `"TypeError"` or `"ReferenceError"` → return `"A JavaScript runtime error was detected. Read the error message and stack trace. Fix only the specific line reported. Do not modify unrelated code."`
- If any tool result contains `"ENOENT"` or `"no such file"` or `"cannot find module"` (case-insensitive) → return `"A missing file or module was detected. Use list_files to verify the exact path exists before attempting to read or require it."`
- If any tool result contains `"EADDRINUSE"` or `"address already in use"` → return `"A port conflict was detected. Use run_command with 'lsof -i :PORT' to find the conflicting process. Kill it with 'kill -9 PID' before retrying."`
- Count the number of tool results in the last 6 messages that contain the same error message string (normalize to first 80 chars). If any error string appears 3 or more times → return `"The same error has occurred 3 or more times consecutively. Stop repeating the same approach. Create a snapshot now, then approach the problem from a completely different angle. Consider reading the full file again, checking your assumptions about file paths and variable names."`
- Otherwise → return `null`.

Folder nodes: arrow icon (▶ collapsed, ▼ expanded), folder icon, name. Click: toggle expand/collapse. Expanded state is tracked in a local Map. On expand of a folder: call `api.listFiles(projectId, folderPath)` to load children if not already loaded.

File nodes: file icon (vary by extension: `.js`/`.ts` uses JS icon, `.py` uses Python icon, `.html` uses HTML icon, all others use generic file icon), name. Click: open file in editor (see 4.8.3). File icon color varies by extension category.

Right-click context menu on any node: shows "Rename", "Delete", and (for folders) "New File", "New Folder". The "New File" option opens a small inline input in the tree at that path. "Rename" opens inline input replacing the name. "Delete" shows confirmation modal.

A "+" button at the top of the file tree opens an inline input for new root-level file creation.

File changes broadcast from the presence WebSocket automatically update the file tree state and re-render.

#### 4.8.3 Editor (CodeMirror 6)

Initialize with the following extensions: `basicSetup` (from `'codemirror'`), `EditorView.updateListener.of(update => { if (update.docChanged) markTabDirty(state.activeTab) })`, line numbers, syntax highlighting via `@codemirror/language` and appropriate language modes loaded based on file extension.

Load language modes from CDN via dynamic import based on extension:
- `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`: `javascript()` from `@codemirror/lang-javascript`
- `.ts`: `javascript({typescript: true})`
- `.py`: `python()` from `@codemirror/lang-python`
- `.html`: `html()` from `@codemirror/lang-html`
- `.css`: `css()` from `@codemirror/lang-css`
- `.json`: `json()` from `@codemirror/lang-json`
- `.md`: `markdown()` from `@codemirror/lang-markdown`
- All others: no language extension (plain text)

**Opening a file:** Call `api.getFileContent(projectId, path)`. If 415 (binary), show a non-editable message "Binary file cannot be displayed." in the editor area. On success, set the editor content, add a tab if not already open, set `state.activeTab = path`. Mark tab as clean.

**Tab bar:** Each open tab shows a modified indicator (dot or asterisk) if the file has unsaved changes. Click tab: switch active file, load content if not cached. Click × on tab: if dirty, show "Unsaved changes — close anyway?" confirmation modal. On confirm or if clean, close tab. If closing the active tab, activate the next available tab.

**Auto-save:** Every 2000ms, check all dirty tabs. For each dirty tab, call `api.updateFileContent(projectId, path, currentContent)`. On success, mark tab clean. On failure, show error notification.

**Keyboard shortcuts:**
- `Ctrl+S` / `Cmd+S`: save active file immediately.
- `Ctrl+W` / `Cmd+W`: close active tab (with dirty check).
- `Ctrl+P` / `Cmd+P`: open quick-open file search modal (see 4.8.7).

#### 4.8.4 Terminal Panel

A "Terminal" toggle button in the editor area header shows/hides the terminal. On first show:
- Create `new Terminal({theme: {background:'#000', foreground:'#d4d4d4'}, fontFamily:'JetBrains Mono, Menlo, monospace', fontSize:14, cursorBlink:true})`.
- Apply the FitAddon and call `fit()`.
- Open terminal in the terminal container div.
- Connect WebSocket to `ws://${API_HOST}/ws/terminal/${projectId}?token=${state.accessToken}`.
- On WebSocket message `{type:'output', data}`: `terminal.write(data)`.
- On terminal `data` event: send `{type:'input', data}` over WebSocket.
- On terminal resize: send `{type:'resize', cols, rows}` over WebSocket.
- On WebSocket close: write `\r\n[Connection closed]\r\n` to terminal. Show "Reconnect" button.

Resize observer on the terminal container div calls `fitAddon.fit()` and sends resize message.

#### 4.8.5 Right Panel — Agent Tab

Shows the current agent session's messages. Message rendering:

- **User messages**: right-aligned bubble, dark background.
- **Assistant messages**: left-aligned, accent left border, rendered as plain text (no HTML injection from model output — use `textContent` or equivalent safe rendering).
- **Tool call blocks**: rendered inside the assistant message as collapsible `<details>` elements. The `<summary>` shows `🔧 {tool_name}` with a status icon: ⏳ while running, ✓ on success, ✗ on failure. The expanded body shows the args as formatted JSON, then a horizontal divider, then the result as formatted JSON.
- **Thinking indicator**: three animated pulsing dots shown while `state.agentRunning === true`.

Below the messages: a `<textarea>` (auto-growing, max-height 200px) and a "Send" button. Pressing Enter without Shift submits. The button is disabled when `state.agentRunning === true`.

On send:
1. If no active session, create one via `api.createAgentSession`.
2. Connect WebSocket to `ws://${API_HOST}/ws/agent/${projectId}/${sessionId}?token=${state.accessToken}`.
3. Send `{type:'message', content: textareaValue}` over WebSocket.
4. Append user message to `state.agentMessages` and re-render.
5. Set `state.agentRunning = true`.
6. Handle incoming WebSocket messages:
   - `{type:'thinking'}`: show/update thinking indicator with iteration count.
   - `{type:'text_delta', delta}`: append delta to current assistant message being streamed. If no current streaming message, create one.
   - `{type:'tool_start', tool, args, call_id}`: append a tool call block in "running" state to the current assistant message.
   - `{type:'tool_result', call_id, result}`: update the corresponding tool call block with result.
   - `{type:'done'}`: set `state.agentRunning = false`, close WebSocket, show notification.
   - `{type:'error', message}`: set `state.agentRunning = false`, show error notification, append error message to chat.
7. After each message batch, auto-scroll the messages container to the bottom.
8. Persist messages to `state.agentMessages` and re-render.

A "New Session" button in the agent tab header calls `api.createAgentSession`, sets the new session as active, clears `state.agentMessages`, re-renders.

A session selector dropdown shows all sessions ordered by creation time, formatted as "Session #N — {created_at relative time}". Selecting a session calls `api.getAgentSession` and loads its messages.
